title: Search the scriptures (John 5:31–47)
hookLine: you search the scriptures, yet won't come to me

lines: A MAP IS NOT THE CITY.
cards: You can know everything about a person and still not know them. You can read every review of a restaurant and never eat there, or study a map of a city for years and never walk its streets.
Yesterday's argument in Jerusalem now turns to evidence: who says you are who you say you are? In that world, a claim needed witnesses; the law of Moses said a matter stands on two or three.
So Jesus calls his witnesses, one by one, the way a lawyer would. The last one is a book.

teach.h: JOHN: A BURNING AND SHINING LIGHT.
teach.b: First witness: John the Baptist. "He was a burning and a shining light," and people were glad to stand in that light for a while.

teach.h: THE WORKS, THE FATHER, THE BOOK.
teach.b: Second: the works, the healings and signs, the man walking with his mat. Third: the Father himself. Fourth: the scriptures.
"Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me." There's a puzzle in the Greek.
The verb can be a command, search the scriptures, which is how the King James translators took it. Or a plain statement: you search the scriptures. Other translations read it that way.
Same letters, both readings possible. Either way, the next line is the point: "And ye will not come to me, that ye might have life." Jesus doesn't tell them to stop searching.
His point is about where reading leads.

teach.h: A MAP POINTS TO A CITY.
teach.b: A map points to a city. A letter points to the one who wrote it.

teach.h: THEY ARE THEY WHICH TESTIFY OF ME.
teach.b: In Christian reading, the scriptures are meant to lead to a living person, not just to more knowledge about him. Christians hear this line in different ways.
Some hear it about the Old Testament promises Christians see fulfilled in Jesus. Others hear a warning for anyone who studies: it's possible to know the text by heart and miss the one it's about.

how: Some Christians read a Bible passage every day, and some practice slow, prayerful reading such as lectio divina, listening for God speaking through the text rather than only studying it.

o: judges who decide whether a claim is true
those who vouch for who Jesus really is
people who watched the healing at the pool

games.q: what's inside John 5:31–47 — tap the pairs.
p: a burning and a shining light

s: the Greek of "search the scriptures" can be read as a command or a statement
the King James reads a command; other translations read "you search."
Jesus tells people to stop studying scripture
he says the scriptures testify of him; the point is where reading leads.
Jesus names John the Baptist as one of his witnesses
"he was a burning and a shining light."

games.q: you're on trial in Jerusalem, and the law says a claim needs witnesses. who do you call last?
games.why: after John, the works and the Father, Jesus calls the scriptures: "they are they which testify of me."

practice: Bring to mind a short passage you know, a psalm, a line from the Gospels, a few words from this path, and say it slowly in your head. Instead of asking what it means, ask who is speaking, and what they might be like.
If you pray, ask to meet the one the words are about; if you don't, notice the difference between reading for facts and listening for a voice.

wordCard.voice: Witnesses. Jesus calls them one by one to answer who he is: John, his works, the Father, and the scriptures themselves.

orig.note: Greek: you search, or search! The same form serves for both, so translators must choose.

carryVoice: Your line: the scriptures point to him. A map is not the city. That's day six hundred seven.
